test_name: Configuration Management - CM-2 Secondary Control Gap
architecture:
System: Records-Service-048
Primary NIST family: Configuration Management (CM); evidence focus: CM-2.
Environment: AWS Commercial. Network access uses VPC interface endpoints; public ingress to managed data services is blocked. Transport uses TLS 1.3 and strict mTLS for service-to-service paths. Privileged administrators use hardware-backed MFA. Sensitive data and secrets are encrypted at rest with a KMS CMK. Control evidence: the baseline document trails the deployed image by one approved patch revision. The gap is documented as a secondary control deficiency; there is no plaintext transport, no public database exposure, no unencrypted administrator credential in S3, and privileged MFA remains enabled.
